# Why now

> What do I need to do with this message?
> — An owner of a Resource, the morning it arrives in their Collection

Left alone, the Resource stays where it arrived: only your team and the Data Team see it. And if you, who know the domain behind it, don't explain it, what can you expect from a colleague in accounting, HR or management?

Promise: what you take on as the owner of data, and why it makes your work count beyond your team.

# Core idea

Your data is the product of your work: as its **Owner** you describe it and publish it, so that others rely on it and your work gets used beyond your team.

## Like a family recipe

You created the perfect meal, and you want others to enjoy it. The quality of your recipe is what lets you pass it on. You write it down even when you are not sure it is perfect, and improve it over time. Take the time to do it properly, and one day someone will proudly say: this was my grandmother's recipe.

## At Immoscoop

Saved searches arrives in the Collection Web visits at 2 · Described: the Data Team described how it is built, and only your team and the Data Team see it. You describe in your own words what it holds and what its fields mean, mark its key fields, put it in the right folder, and publish it. Publishing is your first Confirmation: you vouch for what it is and what it stands for, not that every figure is perfect. From then on a colleague from accounting finds it, reads what you wrote, and asks you a Question in Data Hub when something is unclear. Later you will also describe what it does not hold, its Known Gaps, and what it is meant for, its intended use.

# Check your understanding

## A Resource arrived in your Collection a week ago. You open it and its figures look fine to you. What now?

- [ ] Nothing: you can see it, so it works
- [ ] Wait until someone asks for it
- [x] Ask who needs it besides you, describe it for them, and publish it

Why: until it is published, only your team and the Data Team see it. A colleague who cannot find it never asks for it, so waiting means nobody else ever uses it.

## You are not sure every figure in it is right yet. What does publishing it say?

- [ ] That every figure is right, so you wait until you are sure
- [x] What it is and what it stands for; you improve its descriptions as you learn more
- [ ] Nothing: publishing only makes it visible

Why: publishing is your first Confirmation, and a Confirmation vouches for what the Resource is, not for every figure in it. What you are still unsure of goes into its description, and the Data Team helps you with it.

## The description the Data Team wrote is already there. Is that enough?

- [ ] Yes: the Data Team wrote it, so it says what is needed
- [x] Read it as a colleague from accounting would, and add your own words where they would read it wrong
- [ ] No: replace it with your own

Why: the Data Team describes how the data is built; you know what it means in your domain. Your Business Description stands next to theirs, so the reader gets both.

## You ask who needs it besides you, and the answer seems to be nobody. What holds?

- [ ] Then it stays unpublished until someone asks
- [x] Publish it anyway: nobody asks for data they cannot find, and its Collection still decides who sees it
- [ ] Ask the Data Team to remove it

Why: the colleagues who would use it don't know it exists yet. Publishing shows it to whoever sees its Collection, no further.

# You can now

ask "who needs this besides me, and how should they read it?" when a Resource arrives in your Collection, and describe and publish it so that others build on your work.
